FL-FINGER-SDK.title: Build Environment SDK Fingerprint Identified
FL-FINGER-SDK.description: Isolates plaintext software bill of materials (SBOM) configurations, active compiler optimization versions, and base operating system kernel flags from memory headers.

FL-BOOT-HEADER.title: ESP32 Bootloader Header Verified
FL-BOOT-HEADER.description: The system validated the structure, segment distribution counts, and cryptographic magic identifiers of the physical flash initialization sequence bootstrapping block.

FL-BOOT-SIGNATURE.title: Missing Secure Boot Signature Sector
FL-BOOT-SIGNATURE.description: The expected physical signature verification appends for Secure Boot V2 constraints are entirely missing or unpopulated within the high-memory image trailer layout maps.

FL-HARD-ENCRYPTION.title: Hardware Flash Encryption Appears Disabled
FL-HARD-ENCRYPTION.description: The computed global block entropy density scores drop far below production thresholds. Plaintext data blocks indicate the transparent hardware cryptographic flash encryption core is disengaged.

FL-CRED-HARDCODED.title: Hardcoded Static Credentials or Sensitive Secrets Exposed
FL-CRED-HARDCODED.description: Plaintext passwords, high-entropy tokens, encryption keys, or identity secrets were isolated unmasked inside application code space segments, risking offline data harvesting.

FL-CRED-PRIVATEKEY.title: Private Key Marker Found in Firmware
FL-CRED-PRIVATEKEY.description: Asymmetric cryptographic private key structures were isolated unencrypted within the storage map, exposing transmission avenues to decryption or device spoofing campaigns.

FL-CIPH-WEAK.title: Cryptographic Engine Configuration Profile Identified
FL-CIPH-WEAK.description: Identified operational cryptographic primitives. High-risk instances indicate the usage of broken or collision-prone hashing routines (like MD5) that violate compliance policies.

FL-NETW-URL.title: Hardcoded Public Network Endpoint Target
FL-NETW-URL.description: Plaintext Uniform Resource Identifiers, operational hostnames, remote server routes, or protocol handlers are compiled static, exposing infrastructure layouts.

FL-NETW-IP.title: Static IPv4 Address Infiltration Boundary
FL-NETW-IP.description: Hardcoded IPv4 address assignments were extracted from compiled segments. These indicators leak operational destination topologies or development configurations.

FL-NETW-CLEARTEXT.title: Cleartext Network Transport Endpoint Discovered
FL-NETW-CLEARTEXT.description: The firmware utilizes cleartext communication transport protocol endpoints (such as unencrypted HTTP, MQTT, or WS paths), exposing payloads to transit manipulation.

FL-BACKDOOR-PATH.title: Hidden Administrative/Debug URI Path Discovered
FL-BACKDOOR-PATH.description: Privileged maintenance sub-routing paths or diagnostic interface endpoints were discovered compiled within binary strings, bypassing standard security visibility parameters.

FL-OBFU-XOR.title: Potential XOR-obfuscated Data Detected
FL-OBFU-XOR.description: Repeated mathematical single-byte patterns indicate primitive data masking routines are implemented to obscure configuration constants rather than true cryptographic ciphers.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-010.title: Missing Standard NVS Area Mapping
FIRM-ESP32-PART-010.description: Non-Volatile Storage (NVS) configurations are completely absent from the logical partition index framework.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-021.title: Oversized NVS Storage Boundary Region
FIRM-ESP32-PART-021.description: An oversized NVS configuration target space increases exposure surfaces to offline key extraction.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-030.title: Unencrypted Sensitive Data Partition Identified
FIRM-ESP32-PART-030.description: The target partition stores sensitive secrets but lacks hardware-enforced encryption attribute flags inside the registry table.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-040.title: Critical Partition Boundary Overlap Detected
FIRM-ESP32-PART-040.description: Logical partition boundary definitions intersect or overlap, indicating absolute susceptibility to memory boundary overwrites.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-050.title: Broken OTA Topology Matrix
FIRM-ESP32-PART-050.description: The application contains update targets but lacks an 'otadata' control block partition, breaking rollback safeties.

FIRM-ESP32-PART-055.title: Missing Secure Remote Patching Capabilities
FIRM-ESP32-PART-055.description: Firmware relies exclusively on static factory layouts without remote upgrade capabilities.

FIRM-APP-FUNC-GETS.title: High-Risk Memory Operation Verified: 'gets'
FIRM-APP-FUNC-GETS.description: The inherently dangerous function 'gets' was identified in the binary layout, exposing immediate stack corruption surfaces.

FIRM-APP-FUNC-STRCPY.title: High-Risk Memory Operation Verified: 'strcpy'
FIRM-APP-FUNC-STRCPY.description: An unbounded copy operation ('strcpy') was verified, allowing external inputs to corrupt memory sectors.

FIRM-APP-FUNC-STRCAT.title: High-Risk Memory Operation Verified: 'strcat'
FIRM-APP-FUNC-STRCAT.description: An unconstrained string concatenation routing ('strcat') was identified, creating potential execution buffer contamination risks.

FIRM-APP-FUNC-SPRINTF.title: High-Risk Memory Operation Verified: 'sprintf'
FIRM-APP-FUNC-SPRINTF.description: An unsafe format string target variant ('sprintf') missing explicit length constraint parameters was identified.

FIRM-APP-FUNC-MEMCPY.title: High-Risk Memory Operation Verified: 'memcpy'
FIRM-APP-FUNC-MEMCPY.description: A block memory transfer primitive ('memcpy') lacking strict runtime size boundary assertions was verified.

FIRM-APP-UNSAFEFUNC-002.title: Unbounded Format String Parameter Detected
FIRM-APP-UNSAFEFUNC-002.description: An unconstrained string formatting specifier token ('%s') was identified isolated inside code segments.
